questions.question: Explain why a weather warning may fail to save lives, and describe two ways to strengthen the last mile.
questions.expected_answer: A warning may not reach people (no phone, data, electricity or radio), may not be understood (language, unclear impact), may not be trusted, or people may not know what to do or have nowhere safe to go. Strengthen by: using many channels including community leaders, sirens and loudhailers; using local languages; education and drills; identified evacuation routes and shelters; impact-based warnings.

questions.question: Compare hard and soft engineering approaches to flood management, giving two examples of each and one advantage and disadvantage.
questions.expected_answer: Hard: dams, levees, channelisation, storm-water drains; advantage: can control large volumes of water and protect specific places; disadvantage: expensive, need maintenance, can fail suddenly and can increase flooding downstream. Soft: afforestation, wetland protection, floodplain zoning as parks, sustainable urban drainage; advantage: cheaper, work with nature and bring environmental benefits; disadvantage: take time to work and may not stop very large floods.

questions.question: Write a short case study of the April 2022 KwaZulu-Natal floods under the headings causes, effects and responses.
questions.expected_answer: Causes: a cut-off low stalled off the coast drawing moist Indian Ocean air, giving over 300 mm of rain in about 24 hours on already wet ground; homes on steep slopes and river banks, paved surfaces and blocked drains. Effects: over 430 deaths, tens of thousands displaced, homes, roads, bridges and schools destroyed, water and electricity cut, the port of Durban closed, economic losses. Responses: SAWS warnings (not all received), national state of disaster declared, rescue by the army, police and volunteers such as Gift of the Givers, evacuation centres, rebuilding and investigations.
